reasons.emulator:
VERIFIED 2026-06-01: Cumulus VX 2.5.3 boots (hda.qcow2 = ide bus).
Telnet IAC negotiation at start. Login prompt: cumulus login:
REGRESSED, found + FIXED 2026-07-23 (NPX-297) - a real 3-part compounding bug:
(1) bare "pc" resolves to whichever pc-i440fx-<newest> is aliased on the host
(confirmed via `ps aux`: "-machine pc-i440fx-10.2") and this ~2016-era guest
kernel hangs under it (~100% CPU, zero output, 100+ min) - fixed by pinning
"machine" below to pc-i440fx-yakkety, the oldest i440fx variant this host's
QEMU still ships. (2) that older machine type then made libvirt pick a
"256k-compat" NIC option-ROM this host's qemu package doesn't expose on
libvirt's ROM search path, so the domain failed to even start ("failed to
find romfile ... compat-256k-efi-e1000.rom") - fixed via `<rom bar='off'/>`
on every QEMU node's NIC (providers/qemu.py's _build_interface_xml; no
netplex node ever PXE-boots, so the option ROM has no purpose for any
vendor). (3) with (1)+(2) fixed the domain booted the guest kernel fully
(confirmed via `virsh qemu-monitor-command --hmp "info registers"`: RIP in
kernel space, HLT=1 - genuinely idling, not hung) but produced zero output on
the telnet/serial console netplex was watching. Mounted the actual qcow2
(qemu-nbd) and read its real /boot/grub/grub.cfg: the boot menuentry is
`linux /bzImage root=/dev/sda2` with NO "console=" kernel argument at all -
this image's kernel was never configured to use a serial console, full stop;
it only ever outputs to the VGA framebuffer (confirmed by a VNC screenshot
showing a genuine working "cumulus login:" prompt while serial.log stayed
empty the whole time). A same-day attempt to "fix" this by adding a
"video": "none" opt-in (removing the VGA device entirely, mirroring EVE-NG's
`-nographic`) was TRIED AND REVERTED - it does not help, because nothing in
this image's boot chain was ever told to use ttyS0 either; removing VGA just
makes the (still VGA-only) output invisible on every channel netplex has,
including breaking the VNC screenshot check itself ("no console to take a
screendump from"). netplex never edits a user's imported image (no rewriting
grub.cfg), so the correct fix is the one already used for other VGA-only
guests: "console": "vnc" below instead of "telnet" (matching esxi/vtmgmt/
cisco-fmc/cisco-dnac/cisco-catmanager) - this is the one console channel this
image has ever actually produced output on. Separately, image_profiles.py's
disk_bus_for() had NO entry for the "cumulus" vendor token and silently
defaulted to virtio, ignoring this entry's own correct "disk_bus": "ide"
below (that field is only consulted via an explicit per-node override - the
normal boot path always calls disk_bus_for()) - fixed by adding a "cumulus"
entry to image_profiles.py's _PROFILES table; also directly confirmed via a
raw qemu-system-x86_64 repro that this grub.cfg's `root=/dev/sda2` kernel
argument only resolves under ide (which enumerates as /dev/sda) - under
virtio (/dev/vda) the kernel can't find root and panic-reboot-loops. This
image's disk file is misleadingly named `virtioa.qcow2` per the
vendor-images naming convention, but its real on-disk content and baked-in
kernel argument both require ide - do NOT "correct" disk_bus to "virtio"
from the filename alone (that exact mistake was made and reverted once
already this same day chasing this bug).
reasons.nic:
NIC e1000 -> virtio-net-pci (NPX-824, 2026-09-05). Evidence, not a guess: EVE-NG
PRO v7's own production template for this exact image says `qemu_nic:
virtio-net-pci` (docs/reference/eveng-implementation/raw/templates/cumulus.yml), so a
shipping product has run this guest on virtio for years - the driver is in the
image. e1000 is emulated packet-by-packet in userspace and can never use the
kernel fast path; virtio can (vhost-net, NPX-823). Live-booted on netplex before
this landed - run recorded in docs/status/PLATFORM-AUDIT.md NPX-824.
The bare "cumulus" key is an alias of this same dict, so it moves with it.
